slides.title: The Measure Shop
slides.text: Past the Bakery, the street turns into the Measure Shop. Everything here is weighed, poured and measured twice. Small backwards footprints cross the floor, and each one is exactly 10 centimeters long.

slides.title: Measuring is counting units
slides.text: A measure counts how many units fit. This stick is one meter long, and it holds exactly 100 centimeters. Count the marks: measuring length is counting, just like Unit 1.

visual.label: A meter stick drawn as a number line from 0 to 100 centimeters, with a hop showing 100 centimeters equals 1 meter

focus.cue: Counting starts at 0, not at the first mark you see.
Halfway along the stick: the 50 mark.
The whole stick: 100 centimeters make 1 meter.

slides.title: Worked example: the rice sack
slides.text: Rough first: a sack of rice feels like a few thousand grams, not a few hundred. The sack's label says 2 kilograms. One kilogram is 1,000 grams, so count it twice.

visual.label: Bar model of 2 kilograms of rice: one bar named 2 kilograms, and under it the same rice split into two parts of 1,000 grams

focus.cue: The same rice, measured in kilograms: just 2.
One part is one kilogram: 1,000 grams.
Two parts of 1,000 grams: 2,000 grams in all.

slides.title: New name, same measure
slides.text: Changing units never changes the thing itself. A ribbon stays the same ribbon in meters or in centimeters. Only the count changes: smaller units need a bigger count.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words the Measure Shop runs on.

words.means: the fixed amount you count in, like one centimeter or one gram
how heavy something is, measured in grams and kilograms
how much space a liquid takes up, measured in liters
to write the same measure with a new unit name

slides.title: Stretch: tiny units
slides.text: Stretch: a fingernail is about 1 centimeter wide, and 10 millimeters make that centimeter. How many millimeters long is a 4-centimeter crayon? Stretch work is never in the check.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Brain Board at Practice Board and score 3,000 points to finish. It opens straight on your Measures board, and your board saves as you go. Get there your way: lots of easy tiles, or fewer hard ones. Then measure one real thing nearby and say its measure, unit and all.
